chunks: # Installing Buildkite agent on Windows
The Buildkite agent is supported on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016, and newer. You can use either of the two installation methods:

- [Automated installation (using PowerShell)](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows#automated-install-with-powershell)
- [Manual installation](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows#manual-installation)
[Security considerations](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows#security-considerations)
## [Automated install with PowerShell](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows\#automated-install-with-powershell)
## [Manual installation](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows\#manual-installation)

1. Download the latest Windows release from [Buildkite agent releases on GitHub](https://github.com/buildkite/agent/releases)
2. Extract the files to a directory of your choice (for example, `C:\buildkite-agent`)
3. Edit `buildkite-agent.cfg` and add your [agent token](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/tokens)
4. Run `buildkite-agent.exe start` from a command prompt
## [SSH key configuration](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows\#ssh-key-configuration)
See the [Buildkite agent code access](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/code-access) documentation for more details.
## [File locations](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows\#file-locations)
## [Configuration](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows\#configuration)

The configuration file is located at `C:\buildkite-agent\buildkite-agent.cfg`. See the [configuration documentation](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/configure) for an explanation of each configuration setting.

- Set your [agent token](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/tokens), if you did not set it as an environment variable during installation.
- You may need to use the `shell` configuration option. On Windows, Buildkite defaults to using Batch. If you want to use PowerShell or PowerShell Core, you must point Buildkite to the correct shell. For example, to use PowerShell:

```
#Provide the path to PowerShell executables
shell="C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe"
```
## [Upgrading](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows\#upgrading)
## [Git for Windows](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows\#git-for-windows)
While the agent will work without Git installed, you will need [Git for Windows](https://gitforwindows.org/) to interact with Git.

Buildkite does not currently support using Git Bash to run Bash scripts as part of your pipeline. We recommend using CMD (default) or PowerShell 5.x. You can also use PowerShell Core, but be aware of the odd behavior around pipeline upload steps. Refer to [Defining steps: pipeline.yml file](https://buildkite.com/docs/pipelines/configure/defining-steps#step-defaults-pipeline-dot-yml-file) for more information.

On Windows, all commands run as the invoking user.
## [Installing Buildkite on Windows Subsystem for Linux 2](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/windows\#installing-buildkite-on-windows-subsystem-for-linux-2)
You can use Buildkite on Windows through WSL2, but it has limitations. At present (12 January 2022), hooks and plugins both have issues. We recommend using CMD (default) or PowerShell 5.x instead.

To install the agent on WSL2, follow the [generic Linux installation guide](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/linux). Do not use the guides for Ubuntu, Debian, and so on, even if that is the Linux distro you are using with WSL2.
